initialized.note: handshake bookkeeping; the current handshake works without it

item/autoApprovalReview/completed.note: each auto-review already emits a guardianWarning notification, which codex.el renders as a status line with risk and authorization. This would only add structure to information already shown.

item/autoApprovalReview/started.note: only signals the 2-second pause while auto-review runs; the outcome is already rendered, since every review also emits guardianWarning, which codex.el shows as a status line with risk and authorization. Added CGT_FRAMES to codex_gt.py to sample the screen every N seconds and tried to catch the pause; no review indicator appeared in the frames, so there is no captured rendering to mirror. Recorded as not observed rather than invented.

item/commandExecution/outputDelta.note: the CLI does not display streaming command output. Captured twice: during a 14s sleep it showed only its Working status line, and for an interactive python3 it showed '↳ Interacted with background terminal · python3' plus the stdin, never the streamed output. The gap those deltas hinted at -- an interactive command rendering nothing, because it never sends item/completed -- is closed by handling terminalInteraction instead. Streaming here would also double-render, since concatenated deltas are byte-identical to the completed item's aggregatedOutput.

item/commandExecution/terminalInteractio.note: renders the CLI's captured line: '↳ Interacted with background terminal · python3' followed by the stdin. Terminal name comes from the command recorded at item/started, since the payload carries only a process id; falls back to the pid.

item/fileChange/outputDelta.note: the schema states it outright: 'Deprecated legacy notification for apply_patch textual output. The server no longer emits this notification.' Confirmed absent across 7 sessions, including with patch streaming events enabled.

item/fileChange/patchUpdated.note:
fires only with -c features.apply_patch_streaming_events=true, and then carries a strictly poorer diff than item/completed already renders (captured: '@@
-four
+FOUR
' versus '@@ -3,2 +3,2 @@
 THREE
-four
+FOUR
'). Zero events under default config.

item/mcpToolCall/progress.note: Codex accepts MCP progress and does not forward it. Proved with a probe MCP server: Codex sent progressToken 1 and the server logged 5 successful notifications/progress during a 5s tool call; not one reached the client.

item/permissions/requestApproval.note: captured CLI prompt: 'Would you like to grant these permissions?' with Environment, Reason and Permission rule lines, and four keyed choices -- y turn, r turn with strict auto review, a session, d deny. Those map onto the reply's scope and strictAutoReview. The reply carries no decision: granting echoes the requested profile back, denying returns an empty one. Capturing it needed CGT_APPROVAL=on-request (the harness default 'never' auto-denies before any prompt) plus -c approvals_reviewer=user and -c features.request_permissions_tool=true.

item/plan/delta.note: belongs to plan mode, which an app-server client cannot enter in 0.145.0: the only schema entry point (CollaborationMode) is referenced by no request. turn/plan/updated, already handled, covers the update_plan checklist. Zero events including with -c collaboration_mode=plan.

item/reasoning/textDelta.note: zero events across 7 sessions, including with -c show_raw_agent_reasoning=true. Raw chain-of-thought is not delivered for this ChatGPT-auth model; reasoning items arrive as {summary:[],content:[]}. item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta, already handled, is what actually streams.

item/started.note: not rendered -- the CLI renders items on completion. Used only to record a commandExecution's command, so terminalInteraction can name the terminal as the CLI does.

item/tool/call.note: server->client request for a dynamic tool the CLIENT registered. DynamicToolSpec is referenced by no request in the 0.145.0 surface, so nothing codex.el can send would make this arrive.

item/tool/requestUserInput.note: implemented from the app-server schema, which is authoritative for the request and reply shapes. The CLI's own presentation was NOT captured: no configured tool asks this and no listed experimental feature enables it (checked experimentalFeature/list), so no trigger was found. Prompt wording is this client's own and has not been diffed against the CLI.

thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction.note: blocked: params require echoing back a GuardianAssessmentEvent, which the schema leaves untyped ('Serialized codex_protocol::protocol::GuardianAssessmentEvent'). thread/archived.note: emits {threadId} right after the thread/archive response. Redundant for codex.el's own /archive, which already reports from the response. thread/attachment/add.note: Triaged 2026-09-19 against the 0.155.1 schema and client source; no live CLI capture. Adds a durable stored resource association, such as a pull request identity, independently of conversation history. No resource-association UI; this is not prompt image/file delivery. Confirmed by the upstream app-server README at rust-v0.155.1.

thread/attachment/list.note: Triaged 2026-09-19 against the 0.155.1 schema and client source; no live CLI capture. Lists durable resource associations, including for unloaded threads. No resource-association browser in this client. Confirmed by the upstream app-server README at rust-v0.155.1.

thread/attachment/remove.note: Triaged 2026-09-19 against the 0.155.1 schema and client source; no live CLI capture. Removes a durable resource association without deleting its resource or rewriting history. No resource-association UI. Confirmed by the upstream app-server README at rust-v0.155.1.

thread/attachment/updated.note: Triaged 2026-09-19 against the 0.155.1 schema and client source; no live CLI capture. Reports durable resource association creation/removal. The client neither displays nor caches these associations. Confirmed by the upstream app-server README at rust-v0.155.1.

thread/closed.note: captured by starting a thread, unsubscribing, and waiting: the notification arrived exactly 30 minutes later carrying only {threadId}. Clears the recorded thread id so a later request reports no active thread instead of failing against one the server has forgotten. No CLI rendering exists to mirror -- the CLI TUI stays subscribed while it runs, so its threads are never unloaded this way.

thread/deleted.note: emits {threadId} after the thread/delete response; /delete already reports from the response. Same reasoning as thread/archived.

thread/inject_items.note: programmatic injection, not a user action
